terms.intro: The rules that apply when you use Transcendence, create an account, or play as a guest.

blocks.p: These Terms of Service govern your access to and use of the Transcendence website and game, operated by {company}. By creating an account, joining a game as a guest, or otherwise using the service, you agree to these Terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.
Transcendence is a free, online multiplayer word game developed as an educational project at 42 Paris. The service allows you to:

ul: Create or join game rooms using a room code.
Play as an agent, a spymaster, or a spectator in a red or blue team.
Create a user profile with a display name, a bio, and an avatar.
Add other players as friends and see their online presence.

blocks.p: The service is provided on a non-commercial basis. Features may change, be added, or be removed at any time.

You must be at least 15 years old to create an account, which corresponds to the age of digital consent in France. If you are younger, you may only use the service with the authorization of a parent or legal guardian, who accepts these Terms on your behalf.

**Registered accounts:** To create an account, you provide an email address, a username, and a password. You agree to provide accurate information and to keep your password confidential. You are responsible for all activity carried out through your account, and you must notify us promptly of any unauthorized use.

**Guest access:** You may play without an account by choosing a guest name. Guest names are stored only in your browser for the duration of your session and are not linked to a permanent profile. Guest progress is not saved.
When using the service, you agree not to:

ul: Choose a username, display name, bio, or avatar that is offensive, hateful, discriminatory, sexually explicit, or that impersonates another person.
Harass, threaten, or abuse other players.
Cheat, including by sharing spymaster information with agents through external means or by exploiting bugs.
Attempt to access accounts, data, or systems that you are not authorized to access, or interfere with the operation or security of the service.
Use bots, scripts, or automated tools to interact with the service, unless expressly permitted.
Use the service for any unlawful purpose.

blocks.p: You remain the owner of the content you submit, such as your display name, bio, and avatar. By submitting it, you grant {company} a non-exclusive, free, worldwide licence to host, store, and display that content solely for the purpose of operating the service, for as long as it remains on the service. You confirm that you hold the necessary rights to the content you submit. We may remove any content that breaches these Terms.

The service, including its source code, design, graphics, and word lists, is the property of {company} or its contributors, unless stated otherwise. You may not copy, modify, distribute, or reuse any part of the service without prior permission, except as permitted by law or by an applicable open-source licence.

We process your personal data in accordance with our {privacyPolicy} and our {gdprPolicy}, which describe what data we collect, why we collect it, how long we keep it, and how you can exercise your rights, including your right to access, correct, and delete your data.
You may stop using the service at any time and request the deletion of your account by contacting us at {email}.

We may suspend or delete an account, or remove a player from a game, if these Terms are breached, after informing the user where possible and proportionately to the seriousness of the breach. Account deletion results in the erasure of the associated personal data, except where retention is required by law.

As an educational project, the service is provided "as is" and "as available". We do not guarantee that it will be uninterrupted, error-free, or permanently available, and game data may be lost, for example when the server restarts. Nothing in these Terms limits liability that cannot be limited under applicable law, nor your rights as a consumer.

Contact details, such as your email address and phone number.
Account information required to create and manage your user account.
Technical information, such as your IP address, browser type, device information, and technical logs, where collected.

Create and manage user accounts.
Respond to inquiries and provide customer support.

4.content: We retain personal data only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected, subject to applicable legal retention requirements. Retention periods depend on the category of data and the purpose of processing.

gdprPage.label: Legal & Compliance
gdprPage.title: GDPR Compliance Policy
gdprPage.intro: Our approach to personal data protection, privacy rights, and compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation.

1.title: 1. Introduction
1.content: The 42 Chosen is committed to protecting personal data and respecting the privacy rights of individuals. This GDPR Compliance Policy describes the principles and procedures we follow to protect personal data in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), where applicable.

2.title: 2. Scope of This Policy
2.content: This policy applies to personal data processed by The 42 Chosen in connection with our website, application, products, services, and business operations. It applies to employees, contractors, and service providers who process personal data on our behalf, to the extent relevant to their roles and contractual obligations.

3.title: 3. Principles of Data Processing
3.intro: We aim to process personal data in accordance with the following GDPR principles:

points.text: Data is processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently.
Data is collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes.
Only data that is necessary for the intended purpose is collected.
Reasonable steps are taken to keep personal data accurate and up to date.
Data is not retained longer than necessary, subject to legal requirements.
Appropriate safeguards are used to protect personal data.
We aim to demonstrate compliance with applicable data protection requirements.

4.title: 4. Lawful Bases for Processing
4.intro: We process personal data only where an appropriate legal basis exists under Article 6 of the GDPR. Depending on the purpose, this may include:

points.text: Where an individual has freely given consent to a specific processing activity.
Where processing is necessary to perform a contract or take requested pre-contractual steps.
Where processing is required to comply with applicable law.
Where our legitimate interests do not override the individual's rights and freedoms.
Where the applicable legal conditions for these bases are met.

4.outro: The applicable legal basis is determined for each processing purpose and communicated where required.

5.title: 5. Data Subject Rights
5.intro: Subject to the conditions and exceptions set out in the GDPR, individuals may exercise the following rights:
points: Right of access to personal data.
Right to rectification of inaccurate data.
Right to erasure, also known as the right to be forgotten.
Right to restriction of processing.
Right to data portability, where applicable.
Right to object to certain processing activities.
Rights relating to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, where applicable.
Right to withdraw consent where processing relies on consent.
5.outro: We will respond within the time limits required by applicable law. Under the GDPR, the usual deadline is one month, subject to permitted extensions and notification requirements.

6.title: 6. Data Security
6.content: We implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures designed to protect personal data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure, or unauthorized access. Depending on the risks involved, these measures may include access controls, encryption, secure backups, staff training, and regular security reviews. The measures implemented must reflect our actual systems and practices.

7.title: 7. Data Retention
7.content: Personal data is retained only for as long as necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, unless a longer period is required or permitted by law. Retention periods are determined according to the type of data, the processing purpose, applicable legal obligations, and relevant limitation periods. Data that is no longer required is securely deleted or anonymized, where appropriate.

8.title: 8. Data Processors and Third Parties
8.content: We may engage third-party service providers to support our operations, such as hosting, infrastructure, analytics, customer support, or payment processing providers. Where a provider acts as a processor on our behalf, we implement the contractual arrangements required by Article 28 of the GDPR, where applicable. We take appropriate steps to assess providers and limit their access to the personal data needed to perform their services.

9.title: 9. International Data Transfers
9.content: Where personal data is transferred outside the European Economic Area, we ensure that an appropriate transfer mechanism and safeguards are in place when required by Chapter V of the GDPR. Depending on the circumstances, this may include an adequacy decision, Standard Contractual Clauses, and supplementary measures where necessary.

10.title: 10. Personal Data Breaches
10.content: We maintain procedures for identifying, assessing, documenting, and responding to personal data breaches. Where required by the GDPR, we notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours after becoming aware of the breach. Affected individuals are informed without undue delay where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms, subject to applicable exceptions.

11.title: 11. Data Protection by Design and Default
11.content: We aim to incorporate data protection into the design and development of our products, services, and processes. Where appropriate, we apply data minimization, access restrictions, privacy-friendly settings, and other safeguards from the earliest stages of development and throughout the data lifecycle.

12.title: 12. Data Protection Impact Assessments
12.content: Where a type of processing is likely to result in a high risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, we assess whether a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is required under Article 35 of the GDPR. Where required, the assessment is completed before the relevant processing begins.

13.title: 13. Children's Personal Data
13.content: Where our services involve children's personal data, we apply appropriate safeguards and comply with the additional legal requirements applicable to children. Where consent is relied upon for an online service offered directly to a child, the applicable rules on parental authorization and the age of consent are taken into account.

14.title: 14. Cookies and Consent
14.content: Where cookies or similar technologies require consent, we provide appropriate information and obtain valid consent before activating the relevant technologies. Any exemptions from consent are assessed according to the applicable rules.

15.title: 15. Responsibilities and Accountability
15.content: The 42 Chosen is responsible for implementing the data protection measures applicable to its activities. Responsibilities may include maintaining records of processing where required, reviewing security measures, managing data subject requests, assessing suppliers, and providing relevant staff training. A Data Protection Officer (DPO) will be appointed where legally required.

16.title: 16. Complaints and Supervisory Authorities
16.content: Individuals who believe their personal data has been processed unlawfully may contact us using the details below. They also have the right to lodge a complaint with a competent supervisory authority, in particular in the EU Member State of their habitual residence, place of work, or the place of the alleged infringement, subject to applicable rules. In France, the supervisory authority is the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL).

17.title: 17. Policy Updates
17.content: We may update this policy to reflect changes in our operations, technical measures, or legal requirements. The latest version will be published on this page with its revision date.

18.intro: For questions about this policy or our personal data protection practices, please contact:
